title: Introduce compact edge RAG miniserver with offline tool-adapter and quickstart
author: Anjali Rao
description:
Motivation: provide a lightweight, reproducible RAG quickstart that runs on edge devices or developer laptops with no cloud dependency. This PR introduces a compact Node-based miniserver (minirag-server) plus an offline tool-adapter that lets authors simulate tool-calls locally (shell-safe sandbox + plugin interface). The goal is a tiny end-to-end example for teams who want to vet RAG behaviors, tool-calling integration, and telemetry on constrained hosts before deploying to Redwood Dedicated/Private.

What changed: - new quickstart under examples/edge-miniserver-quickstart with a README, devcontainer, and smoke tests - minirag-server implementation (small Node + sqlite index) that demonstrates prefix-caching, incremental vector ingestion, and local KV caching heuristics - offline-tool-adapter: shims tool calls to either a sandboxed script runner or a pluggable WASM adapter; safe default is a read-only file metadata tool and an HTTP URL fetcher stub - TypeScript client example showing how to call Redwood-compatible REST routes (generation + embeddings + rerank) against the local miniserver - CI workflow that runs the devcontainer-based smoke test and a small integration harness in GitHub Actions - docs/quickstart.md updates linking the new quickstart and describing best practices for edge evaluation

Checklist: - [x] quickstart README with step-by-step local run - [x] devcontainer for reproducible dev environment - [x] minimal telemetry probes (token counts, latencies) - [x] smoke CI that spins up server and runs a seeded RAG query - [x] safety defaults for tool adapter (no arbitrary shell by default)

Why this is different from existing examples: this quickstart focuses on tiny-resource runtimes and explicit offline tool-binding semantics rather than cloud-hosted indexers or full orchestration. The miniserver deliberately surfaces small-scale batching and KV-cache heuristics (configurable) so users can iterate locally on request routing and cache strategies before scaling to Redwood Dedicated.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the offline-tool-adapter API (examples/edge-miniserver-quickstart/offline-adapter/README.md) — I sketched a WASM plugin ABI and a plaintext script shim. If we want to include a compiled WASM sample I can add it in a follow-up; for now the harness uses the safe shims. Also the sqlite index is intentionally tiny (single-file) and includes a simple nearest-neighbor fallback when no embeddings service is available. This behavior is toggled in config/dev.conf.

Related: ENG-1248 (edge quickstart initiative), ENG-1299 (tool-calling safety review).

release_notes: Added 'Edge Miniserver' quickstart: a compact RAG example with offline tool adapter, devcontainer, and smoke CI for local evaluation. Ideal for prototyping RAG behaviors on constrained hosts.
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally includes a tiny sqlite index and a conservative offline-adapter. If we later add a WASM sample, keep it in examples/edge-miniserver-quickstart/offline-adapter/wasm/ and gate inclusion behind an opt-in flag to avoid release bloat.
